why: Every published cost figure rests on a chars-per-token proxy. It was 4 for both rungs, retyped, and never measured. These are the only real measurements this repo has: four billed responses from the two held-out exam runs. They show the error is NOT one multiplier — it is PER MODEL, and the two rungs err in OPPOSITE directions.
no_tokenizer_endpoint: OpenRouter documents no /tokenize or /count_tokens endpoint; token counts come back only as a byproduct of a billed completion (checked 2026-08-27). A proxy is therefore unavoidable — but it can be measured and bounded rather than guessed.

samples.how: DERIVED — prompt length from the code path (window capped at LOCALIZE_WINDOW, `codes` empty), not from the filing, which was not read. Its effect is only to LOWER the bound, i.e. to make costs more conservative, never less.
REPORTED — prompt_chars back-derived from the orchestrator's stated chars/4+250 proxy prediction of 290,825; c-2025 was not read.

rule: PUBLISHED = the MINIMUM observed chars/token per model, rounded DOWN to 1 dp. Minimum, because fewer chars per token means MORE tokens for the same text, so the minimum is the conservative end: it cannot understate a cost. Rounded down for the same reason.
conservative_unmeasured_note: DeepSeek V4 Pro became the first rung on 2026-08-30 without a paid calibration call. The 0.25 chars/token bound deliberately budgets up to four input tokens per normalized-text character; it is a cost ceiling, not a measured tokenizer estimate. Replace it with the same two-sample measured rule after ordinary billed traffic exists; do not spend a call only to calibrate it.
honesty: TWO samples per model. That is thin, and it is a bound rather than an estimate precisely because it is thin. Both samples for each model come from the same two documents, both SEC filings in HTML-derived normalized text, so nothing here says what the ratio would be on a different corpus. Re-derive when more billed responses exist.
